How Jilly Cooper’s Rivals and Autumn Trends are Reshaping the British Heritage Look

The classic British heritage look is currently experiencing a prominent resurgence in fashion, drawing inspiration from traditional country aesthetics and the visual style of screen adaptations like Jilly Cooper’s Rivals.

The Return of Country Classics

In fashion terms, traditional British style relies heavily on utilitarian garments historically associated with rural life. Items such as waxed jackets, chunky knitwear, tartan, tweed, and wellington boots form the foundation of this aesthetic. According to style commentary from fashion analysts, these pieces remain popular because they combine practicality with a rich cultural backstory encompassing history, class associations, and distinct eccentricity.

This season, traditional outerwear brands including Barbour and Mulberry have taken prominent roles alongside Burberry during London Fashion Week. High-profile advertising campaigns have further elevated the profile of countryside-coded apparel, featuring public figures like Kate Moss, Sienna Miller, and Idris Elba styled in classic outdoor wear.

The Influence of Screen Adaptation

The aesthetic revival has been bolstered by the television adaptation of Rivals. Costume designer Ray Holman incorporated original 1980s pieces from heritage labels alongside Liberty fabrics and polo-inspired motifs. This styling has helped reintroduce the classic 'Sloane Ranger' archetype back into contemporary fashion conversations, presenting a nostalgic and semi-parodic take on traditional British wardrobes.

Styling approaches for the look often pair formal or glamorous elements—such as pearls, silk scarves, jewel-toned velvets, and polka dots—with rugged outdoor garments. A common styling choice highlighted in current trends is wearing a battered waxed jacket over party attire or combining tweed with casual items like band T-shirts or baggy jeans.

Practical Implications and What Readers Can Verify

Unlike high-maintenance fashion movements, the British heritage look is often characterized by a preference for a lived-in appearance. Garments like waxed jackets and cashmere knitwear can benefit visually from creasing and regular use, making thrift and charity shop finds viable alternatives to brand-new catalog items.
